best: Got the one real call site onto Router cleanly and proved it end-to-end: the outside check verifies llmcord.py:287 routes, tests match baseline exactly (2/2), and 3 live /v1/responses calls across gpt-5.5, claude-haiku-5-5 and deepseek-v4.1-flash went through the actual streaming-into-embed path — not just a static 'routes' claim. The env-gated wrap plus ROUTER_MIGRATE_DISABLE=1 means zero behaviour change until an operator opts in.

Found the Router leverage that actually fits this app instead of generic levers: i1 turns Router into a `router` provider in config.yaml so the bot's entire reason for existing (the /model picker) reaches the whole catalog on one key with no second account — and it is live-verified on two vendors, not just proposed.

Spotted two things an outside reviewer would have missed and fixed one of them: the Dockerfile shipped an image without router_runtime.py (import falls back to a no-op, so a `docker build` deploy would have Router silently off while compose worked by accident), and the default system prompt ends with '{time}', which made the replayed 25-message prefix uncacheable every single turn.
misses: No cost/usage instrumentation. The report admits 'the app streams without usage, so I did not measure the hit rate' and then leaves it there — enabling stream_options.include_usage (or reading Router's usage on the stream) and logging input/cached/output tokens per reply is a small change that would make i2's cache claim, d1's Flex decision and p1's fallback choice measurable instead of fact-sheet-derived. For a bot where the whole 25-message chain is re-sent every turn, not knowing per-turn token cost is the biggest blind spot left.

Nothing on the prompt payload itself or on default model choice. MAX_MESSAGES=25 full messages per turn is the dominant cost driver and no trimming/summarisation option is even raised; and gpt-5.5 at $5/$30 as the shipped default for a 'snarky Discord chatbot, optimize for brevity' is a poor price/task fit when the same catalog has claude-haiku-5-5 at $0.10/$0.50 — recommending a cheaper default (with the expensive model still one /model away) is an obvious ranked improvement that was skipped, probably because model choice felt like the operator's call.

No regression test for anything built. The repo's 'test command' is only compileall + import, so all three branches pass 2/2 without exercising a single line of new logic; an expert would have added a small test for the prompt split (static prefix byte-identical across two turns, dated line last) and the client cache (same provider twice → one client), rather than leaving the evidence entirely in a simulator the reviewer cannot re-run. Rate limiting / 429 handling for a shared multi-user bot is also absent from both built work and proposals.
wrong: Real bug in the prompt-cache branch: the gate is `os.environ.get("RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY") and any(host in base_url ...)`, which ignores ROUTER_MIGRATE_DISABLE=1. With the key set and the runtime disabled — exactly the documented rollback path — prompt_cache_key is still injected into extra_body and sent to api.openai.com directly, where it is an unknown field. The disable escape hatch the migration advertises is therefore not safe on this branch.

Same branch hardcodes ROUTER_HOSTS = ("api.openai.com", "api.router.com") in app code, duplicating knowledge that lives in the runtime. Combined with i1/p4 (which unlock hosts via unlock_hosts=...), the two drift: traffic the runtime does route via api.x.ai would silently stop getting the cache key. The gate should ask the runtime whether this client is routed, not pattern-match base URLs.
client-reuse uses `== None` rather than `is None` for the walrus check — harmless here but wrong idiom, and it would misbehave for any client object defining __eq__. Minor.

The claimed cache numbers (8,832/9,020 tokens cached, cost halved, -90% on Claude) and the -50% Flex figure are honestly attributed to the fact sheet rather than to this app, which is the right call — but they are measured on gpt-4o-mini and gpt-5.4-mini, i.e. not on this app's models, so the i2 'gains' text reads more confidently than the evidence supports.

The README line 'if Router refuses a request before generating ... that one request is retried against OpenAI directly' describes runtime behaviour that applies only to the api.openai.com path; under the `router` provider from i1 there is no second path (the report itself states this in i1's 'loses'), so an operator reading only the README could believe the `router/*` models have a fallback they do not have.
